note: Pre-registered BEFORE any backtest data was fetched or run (CLAUDE.md honesty rule). Do not edit; a change is a new version with a new fixed_at, and every version's results are published.
signal: count of outgoing transfers from the exchange's hot-wallet set to any address outside the exchange's own labelled address set (native ETH transfers + ERC-20 transfers of the tokens below)
tokens_why: fixed allow-list so fake 'address poisoning' Transfer events (spam tokens that emit from=hot wallet) are never counted
baseline: for each hour, the counts of the same hour-of-day on each of the previous 28 days (28 samples)
baseline_change_vs_prd: PRD said hour-of-week; 28 days gives only 4 samples per hour-of-week, too few for a stable median, so hour-of-day (28 samples) is used. Recorded here before running.
stall_rule: an hour is a stall hour if count < K x median(baseline) and median(baseline) >= 4
alarm_rule: alarm fires at the END of the N-th consecutive stall hour
event_window: from T-7 days to T+2 days, T = the exchange's own stated halt time
controls: two 7-day windows per event that end 35 days and 63 days before T; the alarm must not fire in them

sweep_as_control_only.rule: published as a robustness table; never used to choose the headline parameters

result_metrics: alarm_time - T in hours (negative = before the exchange said it)
alarm_time - first abnormal on-chain transfer, where known
